institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I decidede to go NTNU - Trondheim because of the nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: NTNU provides a lot of information on their website. They can be a bit slow to answer emails during the summer.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is an introduction week for all exchange students and for the study programe we followed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: You dont need to stress about finding housing. I found mine two weeks before i left. You do not get any help from the university to get accommrndations if you are from scandinavia. I ended up paying a lot more in rent than the people staying in the student villages. I belive you can be more lucky than me and pay less.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Just like in copenhagen there is campuses all over the city so its not a problem to live off campus in that sence everybody does it also the ones that live in housing organised by the univerisity.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is easy. You have yo uploade a few dokuments and thats it. You choose some courses but those are not the ones that you need to take in the end. You can easily change which courses you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write them an email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We had some problem with registration for one class but we wrote them an email and then they said it was fine for us to take the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It works a lot like university of copenhagen. The level is in generel a litlle bit lower.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
On master level i took: KLH3101 Obesity: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Consequenses, MOL3000 Introduction to Molecular Medicine, MOL3005 Immunology. Immunology was the hardest course and you had to put some work into it but it was also my favorite course. Obesity ended up being a self-study course because we were only 3 students that signed up for the course and it was in norwegian. It still found it interesting but i belived i would have learnt more if there lectures was not selfstudy.   MOL3000 Introduction to Molecular Medicine did not feel like a master course. We have learnt a lot of the meterial before or the new stuff is not on a higher level from what we already know. 

NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience is a bachelor course. We have already learnt parts of the curriculum of the course in the first two years of molbo.

Dont be afraid of taking only master courses - the level is not different from what we already know.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most courses just have lectures. In each course you often have to do either one presentation or hand in a paper. Some courses have class work as well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience
KLH3101 Obesity: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Consequenses
MOL3000 Introduction to Molecular Medicine
MOL3005 Immunology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
MOL3005 Immunology was really interesting and good. 
KLH3101 Obesity: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Consequenses the course was really interesting. Was a bit sad that it became a self-study course so if there are more students that signs up for it i would really recomend it. 
NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience - is good if you want a course on the "easier" side but you still learn some. Also a good option to take it on 15 ECTS points instead of 7,5 to have one course less to focus on.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs but make sure you have a good insurance that will cover if there is any accidents

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and alcohol are more expensive than in denmark. I didnt spend any money on books because we could find them all online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: NTNU have so many different clubs that you can always find something you wanna try out.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different sports club. The ESN network also organize different social events. In generel Trondheim fells like a city made for the students so the student life there is really good and you have a lot of different opertunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
From the begining go on the cabintrips and so on. The time goes by super fast so try and join as much as you want form the begining. 
Get a membership card to samfundet - you do not need it for ESN.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to lofoten if you have more time. There is also a lot of different places you can go nearby trondheim.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Same culture as in denmark so very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just try and be open and go to the social events. It feels a bit eaiser to get to know other exchange studetns and local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are really kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make the most out of it from day one. Before you know it its december and you are going home again. 
Rember when you decide which courses you want also to look at the exams dates. 
A lot feels the same as in UCPH so dont stress about it and take it as a good thing so you can spend the energy on yorur courses, the people you meet and all the experience you are gonna get.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The earlier you start looking for housing the cheaper i think you can get it but dont stress about it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people i met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Its hard to say goodbye to the place and the people you meet there when you go home again.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
